description: ServiceMatch STANDARD CLASS EXTENSIONS — ServiceNow classes a destination does not ship that discovery sources need; each is a proposal the customer's administrator creates under their own scope (u_ prefix). Mirrors back_end/cmdb/class_extensions.py (every published entry equals its bundled twin). Check ServiceNow's base CMDB, the CMDB CI Class Models store app and OT Manager before adding one; where a shipped class exists outside the base CMDB the entry's `alternatives` names it.

extensions.name: u_cmdb_ci_sensor
extensions.label: Sensor
extensions.why: A sensor that watches a piece of equipment (temperature, humidity, door, motion). ServiceNow ships no sensor class in the base CMDB and none in the CI Class Models IoT family; without this the records of an environmental-monitoring platform have nowhere to go but review.

fields.name: serial_number
fields.label: Serial number
fields.note: the radio or hardware id (LoRaWAN EUI-64 for SensorHubb) — the identity shared with readings and alerts

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.note: the site label; names collide across sites, never identity

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.note: the SITE — a sensor belongs to the site, never to a gateway

fields.name: u_sensor_type
fields.label: Sensor type
fields.note: the measurement channel (TEMPERATURE, HUMIDITY, DOOR …)

fields.name: u_equipment_type
fields.label: Equipment watched
fields.note: what the sensor watches (WALK_IN_FREEZER …) — the equipment itself is not a CI

fields.name: u_observed_by
fields.label: Observed by
fields.note: the platform that reports the unit

identification.note: inherits Hardware's serial-number identification; the EUI is the serial

extensions.excluded_why: coverage before condition: the unit exists and is observed; its condition stays in the platform

extensions.name: u_cmdb_ci_lab_instrument
extensions.label: Laboratory instrument
extensions.why: A laboratory instrument (chromatograph, balance, plate reader, spectrometer, incubator, freezer monitor) in a regulated estate. No discovery agent runs on it: the instrument is known to the chromatography data system or LIMS that drives it, to the calibration register, and to nobody else. ServiceNow ships no class for it in the base CMDB and none in the CI Class Models store app (cmdb_ci_hc_device is a patient-facing healthcare device, cmdb_ci_manufacturing a factory asset, and the store app's own class map sends 'measurement systems' to the generic cmdb_ci_iot parent). Without this the instrument fleet that a GxP change board governs most closely is the one the CMDB cannot see.

fields.name: serial_number
fields.label: Serial number
fields.note: the manufacturer serial on the instrument plate — the identity the calibration register and the vendor service record share

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.note: the lab asset label (e.g. HPLC-07); labels are reused across sites, never identity

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.note: the laboratory / room the instrument is qualified in

fields.name: u_instrument_type
fields.label: Instrument type
fields.note: what it measures or does (HPLC, GC-MS, BALANCE, PLATE_READER, INCUBATOR …)

fields.name: u_controlling_system
fields.label: Controlling system
fields.note: the CDS / LIMS / instrument-control software that drives it — the system that knows the instrument exists

fields.name: u_gxp_relevant
fields.label: GxP relevant
fields.note: whether changes to it go through the regulated change board; a governance flag, not a condition

identification.note: inherits Hardware's serial-number identification; the plate serial is the identity

extensions.excluded_why: the CMDB holds the asset, the calibration register and the validation system hold its regulated state (21 CFR Part 11 / Annex 11) — copying those onto the CI makes two records of record

extensions.name: u_cmdb_ci_access_controller
extensions.label: Access controller
extensions.why: A badge or door access controller — the panel that holds the door schedule and the reader credentials, and the readers it drives. It is on the network (the Thandrel estate had one no agent reported, B542), it has a serial and a model, and a change to it is a change to who can enter a building. ServiceNow ships no class for it in the base CMDB. If the CMDB CI Class Models store app is installed, use cmdb_ci_security (Security Device, under cmdb_ci_iot) instead — but know that it is a bucket: cameras, intrusion detection, YubiKeys and badge readers all land in it, so an estate that has to answer 'which doors does this panel control' still wants a class of its own.

fields.name: serial_number
fields.label: Serial number
fields.note: the controller serial — the identity the physical-security platform and the vendor share

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.note: the panel label as the access-control platform names it

fields.name: ip_address
fields.label: IP address
fields.note: how the controller was seen on the network; addresses move, never identity

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.note: the building / floor the panel secures

fields.name: u_doors_controlled
fields.label: Doors controlled
fields.note: how many doors / readers the panel drives — a count, so the impact of a change is visible

fields.name: u_managed_by_system
fields.label: Managed by system
fields.note: the physical-access platform that configures it

identification.note: inherits Hardware's serial-number identification; the controller serial is the identity

extensions.excluded_why: the CI is the panel, not who may pass through it — cardholders and events are the physical-security platform's record and often personal data

alternatives.ships_in: CMDB CI Class Models (ServiceNow Store, free)
alternatives.note: Security Device under cmdb_ci_iot — the shipped bucket for cameras, intrusion detection and access control; use it when the store app is installed and one bucket is enough

extensions.name: u_cmdb_ci_bms_controller
extensions.label: Building controller
extensions.why: A building-management controller — the BACnet or Modbus device that runs an HVAC plant, a chiller, a lighting zone or a cold room. It is the thing an environmental-monitoring platform (SensorHubb and its peers) reads from and the thing a facilities team changes. ServiceNow ships no class for it in the base CMDB. If the CMDB CI Class Models store app is installed, its own class map sends BACnet controllers, HVAC controls, lighting and leak detection to the generic cmdb_ci_iot parent — a home, not a class; if Operational Technology Manager is licensed, cmdb_ci_ot_plc is the shipped class for a controller that is a PLC, but OT Manager is a paid product built for the factory floor, not the building.

fields.name: serial_number
fields.label: Serial number
fields.note: the controller serial — stable across re-addressing and network changes

fields.name: name
fields.label: Name
fields.note: the BMS object name (e.g. AHU-3-DDC); names are per site, never identity

fields.name: ip_address
fields.label: IP address
fields.note: BACnet/IP or Modbus TCP address as last seen; addresses move

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.note: the plant room / zone the controller serves

fields.name: u_protocol
fields.label: Protocol
fields.note: BACNET_IP, BACNET_MSTP, MODBUS_TCP, MODBUS_RTU, LONWORKS …

fields.name: u_device_instance
fields.label: Device instance
fields.note: the BACnet device instance number or Modbus unit id — unique only within one BMS network, so never the identifier

fields.name: u_equipment_served
fields.label: Equipment served
fields.note: what the controller runs (AHU, CHILLER, COLD_ROOM, LIGHTING_ZONE …) — the plant itself is not a CI

identification.note: inherits Hardware's serial-number identification; the device instance is a network-local address, not an identity

extensions.excluded_why: coverage before condition: the controller exists and is observed; what it is doing stays in the BMS, which is the system of record for the plant

alternatives.ships_in: CMDB CI Class Models (ServiceNow Store, free)
alternatives.note: the generic IoT Device parent the store app maps BACnet controllers and HVAC controls to — a home when one bucket is enough, not a class
the shipped class when the controller is a PLC and OT Manager is licensed
